- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.1) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; cap forecast peaks at +3% above recent 7-day average to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below forecast), reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with trend correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts late-period prices (last 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low swings, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
